data.summary: Station F10 stoppages are driven mainly by missing parts, with equipment/torque faults as a secondary contributor and machine telemetry showing repeated overstrain failures on M-06. The evidence shows part shortages generate the most line stops and downtime cost, while equipment events also stop the line frequently across both shifts. Machine M-06 telemetry confirms recurring failures and high tool wear, reinforcing an equipment-degradation angle.

findings.claim: Missing_part is the top andon reason at F10 and causes the most line stops: 97 stops on shift A and 60 stops on shift B, totaling 157 line stops, far above quality_check which has zero line stops.

Part shortage incidents produce the largest downtime at F10, led by supplier_short on shift A with 423.7 min downtime, 338 cars lost, and 636365 cost, followed by agv_down on shift A with 247.1 min downtime.

Torque faults are the second-largest downtime source at F10, with controller_fault totaling 272.0 min on shift A and 179.7 min on shift B, plus socket_worn and out_of_range variants adding further downtime.
Equipment andon events also stop the line repeatedly at F10: 65 line stops on shift A and 66 on shift B, with counts of 76 and 74 events respectively.

Machine M-06 telemetry at F10 shows recurring failures (up to 2 per day) including overstrain failures and elevated average tool wear reaching 189.7 min, indicating equipment degradation contributes to stoppages.

data.recommendation: Prioritize eliminating missing_part stoppages at F10 by securing supplier replenishment and AGV part delivery for supplier_short, agv_down, mispick, and agv_late causes, since this drives the most line stops and downtime cost; concurrently audit M-06 for controller/torque faults and overstrain failures given its repeated telemetry failures and high tool wear.
